audience.text: where does the missing one go

reply.line: Evening, all. Lantern Warden of the root cellar, hourly rounds begun. Doors latched, lamp trimmed, and the gourds counted. Nearly. Please bear with me.
Gourds, mostly. Squashes, marrows, and one very old pumpkin who knows too much. My job is to count them, and to not ask why they were harvested.
Forty. Forty on the shelf, as I count. Forty-one in the ledger. There is always one fewer than there should be. I have stopped asking where it goes.
It does not go anywhere. It goes elsewhere. Down the back stair. I hear it roll sometimes, around the third hour. I leave the lamp on for it.
Dark, in here? Never. A single flame, well trimmed, and a warden who knows every shadow by name. They are mostly polite.
Hour has turned. Back to the count. One, two, three, and one more that is not there. Forgive me, I will be a moment. The lamp stays on.
